findings.summary: Stale behavior text outside the plan's edits still describes routing by rung
findings.evidence: main.rs:237 (drain help): 'Proposals above the limit, or from an unknown role, are listed as waiting for a person'. drain.rs:381: 'It is waiting for a person unless its rung is within its role's limit.' work.rs:77: brief 'Written only when the steward raises a proposal above its limit'. roles.rs:6: 'above its limit it queues a proposal with evidence'. spec.toml OLY-A-18 mechanism: 'work_decisions.rs sends only a proposal above its role's limit to the owner'. approve_in_limit at work_decisions.rs:363 bails with 'is above that role's limit, so a person decides it', which would be false for a briefed in-limit item once in_limit returns false for briefs. The dependents entry 'documented steward behavior' searched only docs/ and lists none of these. Fix: Add these one-line edits to the step that writes the docs (step 11) and to the files list. Make the approve_in_limit message distinguish 'carries an owner brief' from 'above the limit'.

findings.summary: Overloading in_limit makes its name and doc wrong; a separate predicate would be clearer
findings.evidence: in_limit (work_decisions.rs:64-68) is documented as 'whether the role that raised item may change the item's rung itself'. After the change it also means 'has no brief', so a briefed implementation-rung item reports not-in-limit. split_open and the drain's 'not approved' note then say the wrong thing about why the item waits. Fix: Keep in_limit as the ladder check. Add owner_bound(item) = item.brief.is_some(), and define the drain-approvable set as !owner_bound && in_limit, used by split_open, open_proposals and approve_in_limit. Or, at minimum, rename in_limit or update its doc and every message that cites it.

findings.summary: Unbriefed above-limit proposals already recorded drop off every owner surface when this lands, and nothing says so
findings.evidence: open_proposals, split_open and xtask needs_owner will all exclude existing unbriefed proposals above the limit on athena/records (records from before briefs existed have brief None, per work.rs:78). They stop showing in athena status, the drain's waiting list and decisions.html. Their keys stay in known_keys (steward.rs:1286), so the steward never raises them again. The plan's risk covers new items only. Fix: State in the CHANGELOG entry and D169 that existing unbriefed above-limit items are no longer listed and can be decided only by id. Optionally add a one-line count of them in athena status so they are not lost.

findings.summary: After the change, the recommendation line counts toward a briefed card's word limit and the module doc still says routing is by rung
findings.evidence: Brief::lines() (decisions.rs:170) always adds the derived recommendation. For a briefed in-limit item that line reads 'the steward role may change this itself', which contradicts why the card is shown. html() hides it (line 231), but it still counts toward MAX_WORDS. Lines 20-23 say the recommendation decides 'for the owner to decide' by limit. Fix: Reword lines 20-23 of the module doc to say the page lists by brief. Either drop the derived recommendation from lines() when an owner brief is present, or state that it counts only toward the word limit.

findings.summary: The request description still implies every in-limit item needs a request
findings.evidence: 'What to ask Athena to do, when the rung is at or below your limit.' After step 5, a briefed in-limit item needs no request and its request is never used. Fix: Reword it to: 'when the rung is at or below your limit and the item has no brief'. This is in the same file step 3 already edits.

summary: The plan routes by brief presence in four places: decide(), open_proposals/in_limit, the xtask needs_owner check, and the model-facing words (the prompt and the schema descriptions). I checked it against the snapshot. decide() at steward.rs:693-726 applies any in-limit change and drops its brief, and open_proposals at work_decisions.rs:43 lists every undecided proposal, so the plan changes the code where the fault starts. WorkItem::validate (work.rs:131) needs evidence on a non-blind-spot item, and run() stops on that error (steward.rs:1328), so the evidence on blind_spot_needing_owner is required. The ':owner-action' key avoids the seen-key collision at steward.rs:1322-1325. Every code reader of the changed functions is in the dependents list with a test: status.rs:541, drain.rs:4227, approve_in_limit, xtask needs_owner/read_snapshot, and the audience items, which stay in limit because the audience role is recorded in the same commit (audience.rs:333). All four seeded_proposals callers in drain.rs keep their meaning once HIGH and GHOST get briefs. The schema text 'above your limit' appears only at outputs.rs:320 and no snapshot test pins it. Each demonstration names a seam that exists (the Counting applier, Records::default, steward_scenario/run_steward, the xtask page_with/init_repo helpers, steward_system_prompt/check_budget) and would fail on the current code. What remains is minor: user-facing help text, doc comments and the spec.toml mechanism still describe the old routing; the approve_in_limit error message would say 'above that role's limit' for a briefed in-limit item; in_limit is overloaded; and the change silently hides existing unbriefed above-limit proposals without saying so in the docs. None blocks the plan.
